rationale: The registry unit vt-deferred-written-request declares outputStrategy 'custom_pleading', outputStrategyStatus 'resolved', packetIdentity 'identified' and available true.

The unit description states in terms: "There is no Judiciary form for this request; the statute supplies the destination, the court, the operative facts and the relief, which is what makes a controlled pleading supportable rather than a guess."
The corresponding packetSet component carries no officialFormId and no officialSourceUrl, and none of the ten Vermont forms catalogued in the committed state pack has this role.

Relief is mandatory absent a finding of good cause — the statute says the record SHALL be expunged and the court SHALL issue the order — so the request is a short statement of the operative facts and a request that the order enter, not an argument for discretionary relief.

primaryStatutoryAuthority.description: Except as provided in subsection (h), the record of the criminal proceedings shall be expunged on discharge from probation, absent a finding of good cause by the court, and the court shall issue an order to expunge all records and files related to the arrest, citation, investigation, charge, adjudication of guilt, criminal proceedings and probation.
The deferred sentence itself — the predicate the request rests on: the case ended in a deferred sentence agreement rather than an ordinary sentence.

Notwithstanding the subsection, the record is not expunged until restitution has been paid in full. Carried so the request states the date restitution was satisfied and never asks for relief on an unpaid balance.

The one carve-out from the relief: VCIC retains a confidential special index of deferred sentences for sex offences requiring registration. Carried so the request never asks for relief the subsection withholds.

verificationStatute.description: No verification statute is cited. The registry states notarization: "Not required." That is an affirmative statement that no notarization is needed; it is not a statement that the request is or is not verified, and no source read for this track addresses verification at all. No verification block is rendered, and this gap is carried as a counsel flag in the same way the ND config carries its missing verification statute.

includeProposedOrderReason: Section 7041(e) makes the expungement order the court's own act — the court SHALL issue an order to expunge all records and files — and provides that copies go to each agency, department or official named in it. No form for that order is recorded on this track and no source states an order is tendered with the request. Drafting one would invent which agencies, departments and officials the order names and what each must do. Not drafted.
includeCertificateOfServiceReason: The registry records service as "None by the participant." Section 7608 victim notice does not attach, because that duty is triggered by a petition filed under chapter 230 and this relief arises under chapter 221. No certificate of service is drafted and no prosecutor is named on the request.
serviceNoteReason: No service is required of the participant on this route. The registry records notice as: "The court sends copies of the expungement order to each agency, department or official named in it." That is the court's act after the order enters, not a participant service step, and it is carried in the participant handoff instructions rather than as a service note on the document.
qaProhibitedTermsNote: Three groups, each for a distinct reason. (1) 'petition' and 'petitioner': the controlling scope restriction is that this relief is court-driven, requires no petition, and that anyone who completed a deferred sentence must not be sold a petition packet. A document that styles itself a petition would reintroduce exactly the error the restriction exists to prevent. Note the tension recorded in counselFlag vt-deferred-instrument-label: the registry's own manualCompletionItems says "the petitioner's signature". (2) 'seal', 'sealing', 'sealed': after Act 60 sealing is the chapter 230 remedy; § 7041(e) is chapter 221 expungement and was not amended by Act 60. Using the sealing vocabulary in this request would misdescribe the relief and blur the routing boundary. (3) 'destroy', 'destroyed', 'destruction', 'erase', 'annul': chapter 230 expungement annuls the record and destroys the case file under Court Administrator policies when all docket charges are expunged. Section 7041(e) says the record shall be expunged and that thereafter the court and agencies reply that no record exists; it says nothing about annulment or file destruction, so neither may be asserted here. Scope: these terms are prohibited in the RENDERED DOCUMENT TEXT of this component only. They appear in participant-facing routing and disclosure copy, where they do necessary work — telling the participant that no petition is required and that a petition packet must not be sold to them, and carrying the registry's own disclosure that an expunged or sealed Vermont record may still appear in a federal criminal background check. This is the same split the KY exemplar records.

counselFlags.statement: How long after discharge a Vermont court in practice enters the § 7041(e) expungement order is not established, and therefore the point at which a participant should be told the order is genuinely missing rather than merely pending is unknown. No interval, deadline or 'wait N weeks' statement appears anywhere in this route's participant copy.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The practice interval after discharge before a § 7041(e) order should be treated as missing.

counselFlags.statement: Terminology tension inside the pinned entry. The scope restriction states that this relief is court-driven, requires no petition, and that "anyone who completed a deferred sentence should not be sold a petition packet"; the unit description calls the instrument a "controlled written request". The same entry's manualCompletionItems nevertheless refers to "the petitioner's signature and date on the written request". This route styles the instrument a Request and the signer the Requester, and prohibits the words petition and petitioner in the document text, so the product can never read as a petition packet.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The label a Vermont Criminal Division expects on a § 7041(e) request, and whether 'Requester' is acceptable.

counselFlags.statement: No source read for this track states an accepted caption for a § 7041(e) request. The venue recorded is functional — "the Criminal Division of the Vermont Superior Court that entered the deferred sentence and discharged the person from probation" — and the filing rule is that the request goes in under the existing docket rather than as a new case. The caption is a token pattern filled only from the participant's own countyOfCase and docketNumber answers; the '{county} Unit' form is taken from the committed Vermont state pack's own sample ("Vermont Superior Court, Criminal Division (Chittenden Unit)") and from the state pack filing instruction to file in the Criminal Division for the county that handled the case.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: The caption a Vermont Criminal Division accepts on a § 7041(e) request filed under an existing docket.

counselFlags.statement: No proposed order is drafted. Section 7041(e) makes the expungement order the court's own act — "the court shall issue an order to expunge all records and files" — and provides that copies go to each agency, department or official named in it. No Judiciary form for that order is recorded on this track and no source states an order is tendered with the request. counselFlags.statement: Restitution paid in full is a statutory bar on the relief, not merely a document the participant gathers: "the record is not expunged until restitution has been paid in full." Nothing in this route may be produced, and no request may be sent, on an unpaid balance. Whether restitution is paid is the participant's own answer, checked against a Restitution Unit statement.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That no pipeline stage produces the request while restitution is outstanding.

counselFlags.statement: Subsection (h) requires VCIC to retain a confidential special index of deferred sentences for sex offences requiring registration, listing name, date of birth, offence and docket number, accessible only by the VCIC director and one designated staff person for presentence-investigation purposes. The index survives the expungement, and a registrable sex offence is a self-help stop condition on this track. The participant must be told the index survives.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That screening routes a registrable sex offence out of automated assistance before any document is produced.

counselFlags.statement: Section 7041(e) makes the expungement mandatory only "absent a finding of good cause by the court." A court that has made, or signals it will make, a good-cause finding against expungement is a self-help stop condition. Nothing in this route asserts that no good-cause finding exists or will be made, and nothing predicts how the court will rule.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That a good-cause signal ends automated assistance rather than producing a request.

counselFlags.statement: After 2025-07-01 Vermont is a sealing state, not an expungement state, and participant-facing copy must not use expungement as the umbrella term. Expungement is nevertheless the correct and only term for THIS relief: § 7041 sits in chapter 221, was not amended by Act 60, and its operative words are "the record of the criminal proceedings shall be expunged." The words sealing and sealed are prohibited in this route's document text precisely so the chapter 221 relief is never blurred with the chapter 230 sealing route.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That routing copy elsewhere in the product does not present this track as the general Vermont expungement route.

counselFlags.statement: Scope restriction on this track: "Deferred sentence expungement is court-driven on discharge and requires no petition. Anyone who completed a deferred sentence should not be sold a petition packet." Unit 1 exists to catch this first: on the ordinary path the participant files nothing and the pleading component is not produced at all.
counselFlags.mustConfirm: That orderIssued gates production of the written-request component, and that no chapter 230 petition is offered to a deferred-sentence participant.

Each is rendered as the Requester's own statement. No allegation is generated, inferred or supplemented, and no statement is made about what the court will find.

That the court enter the order § 7041(e) requires absent a finding of good cause — an order to expunge all records and files related to the arrest, citation, investigation, charge, adjudication of guilt, criminal proceedings and probation in the identified docket. Nothing is requested about which agencies the order names, and no chapter 230 relief is requested.
